answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The mine operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay and within 15 minutes, after an accident involving a death of an individual at the mine.

claims.text: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes once it knows or should know an accident has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the accident types requiring this immediate notification.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained so that the incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the underground coal miner for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal/nonmetal mines must hold evacuation drills at least once every six months.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills shall be held at least once every six months to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. This training must be conducted under conditions that, as closely as practicable, duplicate actual underground conditions, with approximately 8 of those hours given at the minesite.

claims.text: New miners must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Training must be conducted in conditions that as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, with about 8 hours given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level (PEL) for noise at a mine is a TWA8 (time-weighted average over 8 hours) of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a noise dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

claims.text: Permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalent to a dose of 100%, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines (30 CFR Part 56), berms or guardrails on the banks of roadways must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air supplied within an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: The breathable air shall sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided regulatory chunks do not contain any information about FAA certification for drone pilots over mine sites. These excerpts cover MSHA (Mine Safety and Health Administration) topics such as site-specific hazard awareness training, mine map certification requirements, certified person qualifications for coal mines, and training record-keeping — none of which address drone operations or FAA pilot certification.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address EPA stormwater discharge permits or runoff from mine sites. They only cover 30 CFR §§ 75.1716, 75.1716-2 through 75.1716-4, and 75.1717, which deal with permits required by the Secretary (via the Coal Mine Safety District Manager) for mining operations conducted under rivers, streams, lakes, or other bodies of water (i.e., tunnel construction/operation near water hazards), not EPA stormwater runoff permits. Therefore, I cannot answer this question from the given chunks.
